breaking changes: New default AOT compatible dependency resolver, remove most AOT labels. (#1461)

* breaking changes: New AOT compatible dependency resolver, soften the AOT attributes

* Refactor tests to use target-typed new expressions and simplify method bodies

- Updated various test classes to utilize target-typed `new` expressions for cleaner instantiation.
- Simplified method bodies by removing unnecessary braces and return statements in async methods.
- Adjusted assertions to directly use the result of method calls where applicable.
- Ensured consistency across tests in handling null checks and service registrations.

* Add comprehensive unit tests for `FullLoggerExtensions` and related logging features

- Introduced new tests in `FullLoggerExtensionsTests` to validate behavior across all log levels (Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal) for standard loggers, generic loggers, and exception-based loggers.
- Added coverage for `StaticLoggerTests` to verify constructor exception handling.
- Expanded `CoverageColorTests` to include validation tests for known color properties.

* Update `FullLoggerExtensionsTests` to standardize null function handling

- Replaced inline `null!` usage with `Func<string> nullFunc = null!` across all test cases.
- Ensured consistency when testing null argument exceptions for loggers at all levels (Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal).

* refactor: improve dependency registration and cleanup within `NinjectDependencyResolver`
- Added null-check handling for contracts in registration methods to enhance robustness.
- Simplified and centralized logic for marking registrations and managing disposables.
- Updated comments and docstrings for clearer documentation and understanding.
- Refactored `GenericFirstDependencyResolver` based classes with improved thread-safety, state handling, and null/unwrapped results processing.

* refactor: improve contract handling and update resolver documentation

- Updated `HasRegistration` to handle null contracts correctly and align with Splat's expected behavior.
- Enhanced documentation in the README to clarify performance and isolation differences between resolvers.
- Added recommendations for resolver usage and detailed performance characteristics for better user guidance.

* Add back the features of the new container table

* Moved logging unit tests to its own assemblies, added missing tests unit tests.

Refactor CompositeDisposable for thread safety and performance (#1477)

* Refactor CompositeDisposable for thread safety and performance

Improves thread safety by introducing a lock for disposal and making _disposed volatile. Optimizes disposal and initialization using Span and CollectionsMarshal for .NET 8+, and refines XML documentation for constructors and methods. Removes unused _count field and updates internal logic for managing disposables.

* Add comprehensive tests for CompositeDisposable constructors

Expanded DisposableTests to cover all CompositeDisposable constructors, including zero and large capacity, empty and single-item arrays, enumerable and non-collection enumerables, and edge cases such as null items. Added concurrency and order-of-disposal tests, as well as tests for large item counts. Updated CompositeDisposable to use Lock on .NET 9+ for thread safety.

fix: scope InstanceGenericFirstDependencyResolver registration callbacks by service key (#1603)

ServiceRegistrationCallback<T> stored callbacks in a single global list and
fired every callback on every registration *and* unregistration, dropping the
(type, contract) scope. Callbacks ran for unrelated registrations and could
trigger nested GetService<T> lookups before T was registered.

Key callbacks by (Type, contract) in a lazily allocated dictionary backed by
the existing lock-free ArrayHelpers.Entry snapshot primitive, invoke only the
matching key, and fire only on Register paths (not Unregister), matching
ModernDependencyResolver. A volatile callback count gives a zero-allocation,
lock-free fast exit when no callbacks are subscribed (the common case), and
per-key snapshots are invoked outside the gate with no per-notify allocation.

Adds regression tests for callback scoping, no-fire-on-unregister, and nested
resolution to both the InstanceGenericFirst and Modern resolver suites.

Resolves #1589.

fix: remove always-false conditions flagged by SonarCloud (#1604)

  always false. Declare it non-nullable (satisfying nullable flow) and remove

- NinjectDependencyResolver UnregisterCurrent/UnregisterAll (x4): the result of
  kernel.GetBindings(...).ToArray() is never null, so `bindings is null` is
  always false. Check only the length.

fix(drawing): keep the aspect ratio when a decode size is requested (#1669)

* fix(drawing): keep the aspect ratio when a decode size is requested

The imaging layer preserves proportions only when exactly one decode
dimension is set, and stretches to fit when both are. The loader set both
whenever the caller supplied both, so asking for a size whose ratio differed
from the source silently distorted the image.

- Read the source dimensions from the image header, without decoding pixels,
  and set only the dimension that constrains the result so the other is
  derived. A source that cannot be measured falls back to the requested
  width rather than stretching.
- Cover the choice of dimension, and add an end-to-end decode that fails if
  a request is applied in a way that distorts.

* refactor(drawing): drop the unreferenced duplicate platform folder

Every file under the folder targeted the Windows presentation stack and
duplicated the folder that already compiles into the desktop targets. No
item group referenced it, so it reached no target framework, and the types
it declared could not serve any other one either. Its size and point
converters still described themselves as Android conversions, which is where
they were copied from.

* fix(drawing): release the source and cover the decode paths

- Set the cache option before the resource identifier, so the image is read up
  front rather than on demand. Without it the loader held the caller's file
  open for as long as the bitmap lived.
- Measure a resource through a stream the loader owns and closes, rather than
  handing the identifier to a decoder that keeps it open. A resource that is
  not a file is left unmeasured, and the decode is then constrained by width
  alone, which still preserves the proportions.
- Cover the measuring, dimension-choosing and resource paths, including a
  request the source cannot fill, a header the codec cannot read and a
  resource that cannot be opened.

fix(drawing): report design mode correctly for nested WPF user controls (#1671)

- Read the design-mode default the designer raises for FrameworkElement
  instead of querying a freshly constructed, unparented DependencyObject.
  The designer only raises that default, so an orphan object answered false
  for any control it did not set the attached property on directly, which is
  what broke a user control nested inside another user control.
- Stop discarding the probe results. DetectDesignMode ran every probe and
  then overwrote the answer with false, so InDesignMode could only ever
  return false. The overwrite has been there since the class was extracted.
- Identify the design host by its process executable, not by the assembly
  base directory. A directory path yields an empty executable name, and the
  containment test matched every name that was a fragment of a known host
  (the empty name included), so the fallback probe reported design mode for
  every application once the overwrite above was removed. The name now has
  to match a known design host exactly.
- Skip host types the target framework cannot load: the .NET Framework and
  Windows-specific targets set UseWPF, so they call the designer API
  directly with no reflection, and the Android and Apple targets compile no
  designer probe at all. Only the target-framework-neutral builds still
  reflect, because a Windows desktop application can resolve to them.
- Drop the Silverlight probe, whose assembly cannot load on any supported
  target framework and which carried the same orphan-object defect.
- Make the memoized result resettable through the existing detector state
  hooks so tests can exercise the class, and cover both detector files to
  100% of lines and branches.

fix(drawing): honour the requested size when decoding on Android and Cocoa (#1673)

* fix(drawing): honour the requested size when decoding on Android and Cocoa

- Decode Android bitmaps in two passes: read the header for the source size,
  subsample inside the decode, then settle on the exact fitted size. The
  decoder writes OutWidth and OutHeight to report what it found, so setting
  them as inputs did nothing and every bitmap came back at full size.
- Decode Cocoa bitmaps through an ImageIO image source bounded by the longest
  edge, so only the pixels that survive the request are produced. Load and
  LoadFromResource previously named the dimensions and never read them.
- Fit a requested box without distorting the image: the edge with the smaller
  scale factor binds and the other follows from the source proportions.
- Extract the arithmetic into BitmapDecodeSize, which has no platform
  dependency, so the contract is unit tested on the desktop targets instead of
  only on platforms no test runs on.

* build: exclude the unreachable platform folders from coverage analysis

The Android, Cocoa and .NET Framework platform folders compile only into target
frameworks no test project builds, so nothing loads them on any machine or CI
leg. Coverage analysis counted them as uncovered new code and disagreed with the
coverage service, which reports only what the collected reports contain.
